title: Stop AI drift
desc: Why an AI that was doing great an hour ago starts making things up, and the five habits that keep it anchored: fresh sessions, written state, verification before belief, and more.
em: Why it was right an hour ago and wrong now.
lead: Drift is when the AI slowly stops doing what you asked: it forgets a rule, invents a detail, grades its own work generously, or solves a slightly different problem than the one you gave it. It is not random. It has causes, and each cause has a fix.
tiles: The four causes of drift and the five habits that stop it.
A reset prompt that re-anchors a session that has started to slide.
Aton's session checklist, the state file template, and the verification ritual.

sections.label: The four causes
body: steps
The conversation got long.
Early instructions get buried under later ones. The AI weights what is recent. Your rule from message three is now competing with two hundred messages of noise.
The state lives in the chat.
If the only record of what was decided is the conversation, the AI has to remember it. It will not.
Nobody checked.
The AI said it did something and everyone believed it. Unverified claims compound. By the fifth one the work is fiction.
The problem changed.
You asked for one thing, then adjusted, then adjusted again. The AI is now solving the average of your requests.

sections.label: Five habits
sections.h2: The habits that keep it anchored.
body: steps
Fresh sessions for new jobs.
When the task changes, start a new conversation. Carry the state in a file, not in the chat.
Write the state down.
A short file: what was decided, what is done, what is next. The AI reads it at the start. You update it at the end. This is the single biggest fix.
Verify before you believe.
'Done' means shown, not said. Ask for the evidence: the output, the screenshot, the test result. If it cannot show it, it did not do it.
Restate the job.
Every few passes, have the AI say back in two lines what it is building and what done looks like. If the restatement is off, you caught the drift early.
Keep the rules in a file.
Standing rules live in the brain file or the skill, not in the chat. A rule in a file survives. A rule in a message fades.

sections.label: Catching it early
sections.h2: Three signs it is already drifting.
body: checks
It starts using words you never used, especially confident ones.
It stops asking questions it used to ask.
Its summaries get more polished while the actual output gets thinner.
said
What the coach says
The summary read like everything shipped. The screenshot showed half of it. Ask for the screenshot first, the summary second.

Three to five. These go in the brain file or the skill, not the chat.
Screenshot, test, output, a person checking. Be specific.
When you start a fresh session
The trigger. New task, new day, after a bad turn.
pr: Re-anchor a session that has started to slide.
Paste this when the AI feels off. It forces a restatement and a check before any more work.
prompt: Stop. Before doing anything else: 1. Restate in two lines what you are building and what done looks like. 2. List every rule you are operating under. If a rule came from a file, name the file. If it came from this chat, say so. 3. List what you have claimed is done in this session, and for each one say whether you verified it (show how) or only believe it. 4. Say what you would change about the plan if you were starting fresh right now. Then wait. Do not continue until I confirm the restatement is right.
